---
Why Your Ideas Are Being Ignored (And How to Fix It)

Most experts have incredible knowledge but terrible communication skills. Their groundbreaking research gets buried because no one can understand what they're trying to say. 

This video tells the story of economist W. Brian Arthur, who cracked the code on how companies like Microsoft, Google, and Facebook dominate their markets—but his revolutionary idea almost died because he couldn't write about it clearly.

Then Arthur did something unprecedented: he asked Pulitzer Prize-winning novelist Cormac McCarthy to help him rewrite his paper. What happened next changed everything. McCarthy transformed Arthur's unreadable academic jargon into clear, compelling prose using the same principles that made his novels legendary. The result became one of Harvard Business Review's most popular articles of all time.

In this video, you'll discover the 12 writing principles McCarthy used to transform Arthur's work from academic obscurity to mainstream success. These aren't just writing tips—they're communication strategies that can make your ideas impossible to ignore. Whether you're writing emails, reports, proposals, or presentations, these principles will help you turn complex concepts into clear, persuasive communication that actually gets results.

Learn how minimalism creates clarity, why every paragraph needs a single message, how to choose concrete examples over abstract concepts, and the surprising grammar rules that make your writing flow naturally. You'll also discover why the best writing advice is to please yourself first, and how that counterintuitive approach leads to better reader engagement.
If you've ever felt like your expertise isn't getting the recognition it deserves, this video shows you exactly how to package your knowledge in a way that people can't help but pay attention to.
